capabilities: Edit Markdown notes in a WYSIWYG view without converting files
Insert blocks and Obsidian structures via a slash menu
Select, drag, reorder, and transform blocks
Apply highlights and paragraph alignment, optionally saved as HTML
Customize toolbar position and button layouts for desktop and mobile
extras: Proprietary, source-visible but not open source; paid with a 15-day trial, after which the editing view becomes read-only (notes stay accessible in other views). Requires Obsidian 1.7.2+; contacts api.buttereditor.com and licenses.buttereditor.com for licensing and feedback. Optional rich formatting (color, underline, alignment) saves as HTML and may be less portable.
intentEvidence: Unlike Live Preview, it keeps supported Markdown syntax out of the editing surface while you write.
problem: Obsidian's Source and Live Preview modes show Markdown syntax while typing, and other WYSIWYG approaches can convert notes or lock them into a proprietary format.

relations.evidence: Many plugins that insert text or show suggestions, such as templates, dates, autocomplete, and Tasks, work inside Butter.

summary: Paid WYSIWYG editing view that renders supported Markdown in place while writing, keeping notes as plain .md files alongside Obsidian's other view modes.
